item.title: Meoto Iwa: The Wedded Rocks of Futami — Guide
item.description: Meoto Iwa, the ‘Wedded Rocks’, are two sea stones off the coast of Futami near Ise, joined by a great shimenawa rope of rice straw and revered as a symbol of the sacred union of the creator deities Izanagi and Izanami — and of marriage and harmony ever since. The larger ‘husband’ rock wears a small torii on its crown, and the pair belong to nearby Futami Okitama Shrine, a traditional place of purification before visiting Ise Jingu.
